cases.title: Corporate donations: keep the group and legal payer separate
cases.summary: IRB FY2023-24 consolidated financials disclose ₹67.62crore in political donations, including ₹30crore to BJP, ₹1.62crore to BalasahebanchiShivsena and ₹36crore in electoral bonds without recipient allocation. Standalone IRBIDL political donations are NIL. Modern Road Makers separately reports ₹35crore political donations without naming parties. IRB MP Expressway reports ₹25crore donations without a political-party label in the reviewed note.
cases.attribution: Company and subsidiary audited financial-statement disclosures; scope control, not an allegation.
cases.response: No wrongdoing is alleged and no response was requested. The company disclosures themselves state the consolidated/standalone distinction. No inference about contract influence or legality is made.
alternativeExplanations: A consolidated group includes subsidiary transactions while a parent standalone account can correctly report no political donations.
Ordinary lawful contributions can coexist with competitively awarded contracts.
cases.falsifier: Obtain entity-level transaction ledgers and original SBI purchase/redemption records with validated bond prefix-plus-number joins; do not allocate party recipients using amount alone.

researchNotes: Original ECI electoral-bond tables not retrieved; no serial-number recipient join published.
IRB legal company is outside the original259-company universe, so no legacy company canonicalId was forced.
Legacy corporate group aliases were not used. Only exact official-office canonicalIds are recorded.
